title: Power Automate: configure Flow checker rules and notifications for desktop flows in the admin portal
summary: The briefing distinguishes the launched roadmap capability from the rule configuration Microsoft Learn documents, and its control paths and licensing prerequisite are supported. Clarify that rule thresholds are already documented, and note the different severity terminology used by the solution checker reference.

claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns Power Automate desktop flows.
claims.quote: Power Automate: Desktop flows - Configure notifications for desktop flow checker in admin portal

claims.claim: The roadmap says that engine loads default and custom rules.
claims.quote: loading default and custom rules to evaluate quality, performance, and maintainability issues

claims.claim: The roadmap's purpose is earlier identification of quality issues rather than discovery through failures or escalations.

claims.quote: Administrators can select the notification type (error, warning, or informational), adjust severity levels, and define parameters such as thresholds, recurrence, and scope.

claims.quote: For desktop flows that are already open in the designer, reopen the flow for configuration changes to take effect.

claims.claim: Admin-centre solution checker enforcement takes precedence over portal Flow checker configuration.
claims.quote: Solution checker enforcement settings that you configure in the Power Platform admin center take precedence over Flow checker configuration settings in the Power Automate portal.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Rules restricted by solution checker enforcement cannot be modified in the portal.
claims.quote: You can't modify rules that are restricted through Solution checker enforcement in the Power Automate portal.

claims.claim: A defined environment-group configuration is inherited and cannot be individually edited.
claims.quote: If the environment is part of an environment group with a defined configuration, the rule settings are inherited and can't be edited individually.

claims.quote: Deleting copied actions after viewing a rule violation detail can trigger unhandled errors.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Whether notifications are sent by default is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop Flow checker notifications default; read roadmap and static-analysis. Automatic enablement is stated, but no default notification sending or enforcement configuration is specified; runtime notifications concern a different feature.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; controls[2].api; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: No Flow checker notification configuration UI or API is documented for notification types, thresholds, recurrence and scope.
claims.quote: Searched: Flow checker notification settings Power Platform API pac admin Power Apps administration PowerShell Dataverse msdyn_analysisoverride. Read static-analysis, msdyn_analysisoverride and pac admin search excerpt; found rule controls, not notification controls.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: Notification delivery channels, recipients and payload are not documented for this checker capability.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop Flow checker notifications configuration default recipients delivery recurrence scope licensing pricing; opened static-analysis. Runtime notifications search excerpt describes run-status pop-ups, not checker-violation notifications.

claims.claim: The Flow checker documentation describes no new data source or external destination.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop Flow checker static analysis rule violations block running flow data external destination notification; read static-analysis in full. No new data source or external destination is specified.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Learn documents no checker step that edits or stops a flow.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop Flow checker static analysis rule violations block running flow data external destination notification; read static-analysis. It describes analysis, violation displays and suggested fixes, not automatic edits or stopping flows.

claims.claim: The Flow checker page does not say whether a rule violation can block a desktop flow from running.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop Flow checker static analysis rule violations block running flow; read static-analysis and solution checker enforcement. The latter documents blocking solution imports, not blocking desktop-flow runs.

claims.claim: Sources do not say this rollout changes existing rule defaults.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop Flow checker notifications default; read roadmap and static-analysis. The page lists rule severities but neither source states that this notification rollout changes existing rule defaults.

claims.claim: Learn's known limitation restricts customisation to enablement and severity, whereas Rule management also describes parameter values.
claims.quote:
Rule customization is limited to enabling or disabling rules and configuring severity.
Configure custom values for rules that support parameters, such as thresholds and limits (Power Automate portal only).

claims.claim: Applying rules to specific environments or environment groups is documented as an admin-centre Managed Environments capability.
claims.quote: Apply rules to specific environments or environment groups (Managed Environments, Power Platform admin center only).

claims.claim: The Object name column in solution checker results identifies the desktop flow responsible for a violation.
claims.quote: Identify which desktop flow triggers a specific rule violation by checking the Object name column in the results. This column shows the name of the corresponding desktop flow.

claims.claim: Desktop-flow makers see analysis violations in the designer.
claims.quote: Flow checker error violations show an inline indicator and a popup with more details. Warnings also appear inline in the designer workspace, like errors.

claims.quote:
select Manage.

claims.claim: GET /msdyn_analysisoverrides is the documented RetrieveMultiple operation on Analysis Override, presented as a table operation rather than a confirmed notification API.

claims.claim: Learn names Analysis Override privileges but does not confirm that the portal stores these settings in that table.
claims.quote: Searched: Flow checker notification settings Power Platform API pac admin Power Apps administration PowerShell Dataverse msdyn_analysisoverride; read static-analysis and searched msdyn_analysisoverride reference for portal, notification, parameter and environment. No storage mapping found.

claims.claim: The roadmap's notification-specific thresholds, recurrence and scope are not described by Learn as notification controls.
claims.quote: Searched: Flow checker notification thresholds; Flow checker notification recurrence. Read static-analysis: rule thresholds and environment scope are documented, but notification thresholds, recurrence and scope are not.
claims.fix: Replace 'the roadmap’s thresholds, recurrence and scope are described only on the roadmap' with 'Learn documents rule thresholds and environment scope, but not notification-specific thresholds, recurrence or scope.' This keeps the notification qualification explicit and avoids implying that rule thresholds are undocumented.

claims.claim: The supplied sources do not mandate administrator action for this notification capability.
claims.quote: Searched: desktop Flow checker notifications default; read roadmap and static-analysis. No mandatory rollout action or act-by date is given; no Message Center post was supplied.
